transliteration_key.g: ج (في مصر تُنطق g مثل gate)

reply.english: Yesterday I went to the market.
Yes, I bought a new shirt.

phrases.arabic: أَوَّل إِمْبَارِح كَان عِنْدِي شُغْل لِحَدّ اَلْمَسَا
phrases.transliteration: awwil imbaare7 kaan 3andi shoghl la7add el-masa

reply.english: I stayed up until two in the morning.
I had a lot of work.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: أهلا منى، عاملة إيه؟
dialogue.transliteration: ahlan Mona, 3amla eh?
dialogue.english: Hi Mona, how are you?

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.arabic: أهلا كريم، الحمد لله تمام. إنت كنت فين إمبارح؟
dialogue.transliteration: ahlan Kareem, el-7amdu lillah tamaam. inta kunt feen imbaare7?
dialogue.english: Hi Kareem, fine, thank God. Where were you yesterday?

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: إمبارح كان يوم طويل أوي، صحيت متأخر وبعدين روحت الشغل.
dialogue.transliteration: imbaare7 kaan yoom Taweel awi, Se7eet mit2akhkhar w-ba3deen ro7t esh-shoghl.
dialogue.english: Yesterday was a very long day, I woke up late and then went to work.

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.arabic: وأول إمبارح كنت فين؟ ماجيتش ليه؟
dialogue.transliteration: w-awwil imbaare7 kunt feen? ma-geetish leeh?
dialogue.english: And the day before yesterday, where were you? Why didn't you come?

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: أول إمبارح كان عندي شغل لحد المسا، اتعبت أوي.
dialogue.transliteration: awwil imbaare7 kaan 3andi shoghl la7add el-masa, it3abt awi.
dialogue.english: The day before yesterday I had work until the evening, I got very tired.

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.arabic: ألف سلامة عليك! وإمبارح بالليل عملت إيه؟
dialogue.transliteration: alf salaama 3aleek! w-imbaare7 bil-leel 3amalt eh?
dialogue.english: Hope you are feeling better! And last night, what did you do?

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: أكلنا في مطعم حلو أوي مع صحابي.
dialogue.transliteration: akalna fee maT3am 7elw awi ma3a S7aabi.
dialogue.english: We ate at a really nice restaurant with my friends.

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.arabic: شفت مين؟ حد أعرفه؟
dialogue.transliteration: shuft meen? 7add a3rafu?
dialogue.english: Who did you see? Anyone I know?

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: شفت أحمد وسامي، وسلموا عليكي.
dialogue.transliteration: shuft a7mad w-saami, w-sallemu 3aleeki.
dialogue.english: I saw Ahmed and Sami, and they said hello to you.

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.arabic: الله يسلمهم! سهرت لحد الساعة كام؟
dialogue.transliteration: allah yisallimhom! sihirt la7add es-saa3a kaam?
dialogue.english: God keep them well! How late did you stay up?

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: لحد اتنين الصبح، والجو كان حلو أوي إمبارح.
dialogue.transliteration: la7add itneen eS-Sob7, w-el-gaw kaan 7elw awi imbaare7.
dialogue.english: Until two in the morning, and the weather was really nice yesterday.

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.arabic: يا سلام! المرة الجاية خدني معاك.
dialogue.transliteration: ya salaam! el-marra el-gaya khudni ma3aak.
dialogue.english: Wow! Next time take me with you.

response.english: I saw my brother and my cousin.

lessons.culture: إمبارح is the everyday Cairene word for yesterday; أمس and البارح sound bookish and are heard in news and writing, not in casual talk. Asking إمبارح عملت إيه؟ is a normal way to open a catch-up with a friend or neighbour.

exercises.prompt: صاحبك بيسألك: "إمبارح عملت إيه؟". جاوبه إنك روحت السوق.

too_formal.feedback: Correct MSA but far too formal for a casual chat; إمبارح روحت السوق is what is really said.

exercises.tip: "إمبارح" is yesterday; the past verb follows it.

exercises.prompt: صاحبك بيسألك: "كنت فين إمبارح بالليل؟". جاوبه إنك كنت في البيت.

too_formal.feedback: Fine MSA, but منزل and ليلة أمس are bookish; Egyptians say البيت and إمبارح بالليل.

exercises.tip: "في" here is fee, and "البيت" is the ordinary word for home.

exercises.prompt: أكمل: "_____ كان يوم طويل أوي." المعنى: Yesterday was a very long day.

too_formal.feedback: أمس is the MSA word; in spoken Egyptian it is إمبارح.

exercises.tip: "إمبارح" opens the sentence, like "yesterday" in English.

exercises.prompt: أكمل: "ماجيتش _____ إمبارح؟" المعنى: Why didn't you come yesterday?

too_formal.feedback: لماذا is MSA; in Cairo everyone says ليه.

exercises.tip: "ليه" = why. The negative is ما + verb + ش.

exercises.prompt: ترجم: "What did you do yesterday?" (تكلم راجل)

too_formal.feedback: Correct MSA, but إيه not ماذا is how "what" is really said in Cairo.

exercises.tip: "إيه" = what, and it usually comes at the end.

exercises.prompt: ترجم: "I got very tired from work yesterday."

too_formal.feedback: MSA is correct but stiff; أوي is the Egyptian "very" and الشغل is work.

exercises.tip: "أوي" = very, put after the word it strengthens.

exercises.prompt: أي جملة معناها "I woke up late yesterday"؟

too_formal.feedback: استيقظت is MSA; صحيت is what is said when you wake up.

exercises.prompt: أي جملة معناها "Did you buy anything yesterday?"؟

too_formal.feedback: هل and شيئا are MSA; Cairo says حاجة and just raises the voice for a question.

exercises.tip: "حاجة" = something, anything, with a hard g.

exercises.prompt: رتب الجملة: (Yesterday the weather was really nice)

too_formal.feedback: الطقس and جميلا جدا are MSA; the spoken words are الجو and حلو أوي.

exercises.prompt: رتب الجملة: (Who did you see yesterday?)

too_formal.feedback: رأيت is MSA; شفت is the everyday verb for saw.

exercises.tip: "مين" = who, and it stays in place instead of moving to the front.

phrases.arabic: لَمَّا كُنْت صُغَيِّر كُنْت بَاحِب أَلْعَب بَرَّه
phrases.transliteration: lamma kunt soghayyar kunt ba7ebb el3ab barra

phrases.arabic: اِتْرَبِّيت فِي حَيّ قَدِيم فِي اَلْقَاهِرَة
phrases.english: I grew up in an old neighborhood in Cairo.

phrases.arabic: كُل صَيْف كُنَّا بِنْرُوح عِنْد جَدِّي فِي اَلْبَلَد
phrases.transliteration: kull Seef kunna benro7 3and gaddi fil-balad

phrases.arabic: تِيتَة كَانِت بِتْحَكِّيلَنَا حَوَادِيت قَبْل اَلنَّوْم
أَوَّل عَجَلَة كَانِت عِنْدِي كَانِت حَمْرَا
كُنْت بَاخَاف مِن اَلضِّلْمَة أَوِي وَأَنَا صُغَيِّر
phrases.transliteration: kunt bakhaaf min iD-Dalma awi w-ana soghayyar

phrases.arabic: اَلْمُدَرِّس بِتَاعِي فِي اَلْمَدْرَسَة كَان طَيِّب أَوِي
phrases.transliteration: el-modarris bitaa3i fil-madrasa kaan Tayyib awi

phrases.arabic: كُنَّا بِنْرُوح المدرسة مَشِي سَوَا كُل يُوم
phrases.transliteration: kunna benro7 el-madrasa mashi sawa kull yoom

phrases.arabic: وَأَنَا صُغَيِّر كُنْت بَاحْلَم أَبْقَى طَيَّار
phrases.transliteration: w-ana soghayyar kunt ba7lam ab2a Tayyaar

dialogue.speaker: Heba
dialogue.arabic: إنت اتربيت فين يا عمر؟
dialogue.transliteration: inta itrabbeet feen ya 3omar?
dialogue.english: Where did you grow up, Omar?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: أنا اتربيت في حي قديم في القاهرة، في السيدة زينب.
dialogue.transliteration: ana itrabbeet fee 7ayy 2adeem fil-2aahira, fee es-sayyeda zeinab.
dialogue.english: I grew up in an old neighborhood in Cairo, in Sayyida Zeinab.

dialogue.speaker: Heba
dialogue.arabic: وكنت بتعمل إيه وإنت صغير؟
dialogue.transliteration: w-kunt bet3mel eh w-inta soghayyar?
dialogue.english: And what did you do when you were young?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: لما كنت صغير كنت باحب ألعب بره، وكان عندي صاحب اسمه كريم.
dialogue.transliteration: lamma kunt soghayyar kunt ba7ebb el3ab barra, w-kaan 3andi Saa7eb ismu kareem.
dialogue.english: When I was young I loved playing outside, and I had a friend named Kareem.

dialogue.speaker: Heba
dialogue.arabic: كنتوا بتلعبوا إيه؟
dialogue.transliteration: kuntu bet-el3abu eh?
dialogue.english: What did you play?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: كنا بنلعب كورة في الحارة كل يوم.
dialogue.transliteration: kunna benel3ab koora fil-7aara kull yoom.
dialogue.english: We used to play football in the alley every day.

dialogue.speaker: Heba
dialogue.arabic: وفي الأجازة؟ كنتوا بتسافروا؟
dialogue.transliteration: w-fil-agaaza? kuntu betsaafru?
dialogue.english: And on holidays? Did you travel?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: كل صيف كنا بنروح عند جدي في البلد، وتيتة كانت بتحكيلنا حواديت قبل النوم.
dialogue.transliteration: kull Seef kunna benro7 3and gaddi fil-balad, w-teeta kaanit bet7ekkeelna 7awadeet 2abl en-noom.
dialogue.english: Every summer we went to my grandfather's in the village, and Grandma told us stories before sleeping.

dialogue.speaker: Heba
dialogue.arabic: الله! وكنت بتخاف من حاجة؟
dialogue.transliteration: allah! w-kunt bet-khaaf min 7aaga?
dialogue.english: Wow! And were you afraid of anything?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: كنت باخاف من الضلمة أوي، وأول عجلة كانت عندي كانت حمرا.
dialogue.transliteration: kunt bakhaaf min iD-Dalma awi, w-awwil 3agala kaanit 3andi kaanit 7amra.
dialogue.english: I was very afraid of the dark, and the first bike I had was red.

dialogue.speaker: Heba
dialogue.arabic: وقتها الدنيا كانت أبسط بكتير.
dialogue.transliteration: wa2tuha id-dunya kaanit absaT bekteer.
dialogue.english: Back then life was much simpler.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: فعلا، ربنا يرجع الأيام دي.
dialogue.transliteration: fe3lan, rabbena yerag-ga3 el-ayyaam di.
dialogue.english: Truly, may God bring those days back.

response.arabic: اِتْرَبِّيت فِي حَيّ قَدِيم فِي اَلْقَاهِرَة
response.english: I grew up in an old neighborhood in Cairo.

pair.english: What did you play when you were young?
Where did you go in the summer?

response.arabic: كنا بنروح عند جدي في البلد
response.english: We went to my grandfather's in the village.

pair.english: What did you dream of becoming?

response.english: I dreamed of becoming a pilot.

lessons.culture: When Egyptians tell childhood stories they use كنت or كنا followed by ب and the verb, as in كنا بنلعب. تيتة is grandma and جدو is grandpa, said at home with close family.

exercises.prompt: صاحبك بيسألك: "إنت اتربيت فين؟". جاوبه إنك اتربيت في القاهرة.
accepted: اِتْرَبِّيت فِي حَيّ قَدِيم فِي اَلْقَاهِرَة

too_formal.feedback: نشأت is literary; the spoken verb for grew up is اتربيت.

exercises.tip: "اتربيت" = I grew up, I was raised.

exercises.prompt: صاحبك بيسألك: "كنت بتخاف من إيه وإنت صغير؟". جاوبه إنك كنت بتخاف من الضلمة.

too_formal.feedback: الظلام is MSA; Cairo says الضلمة, and باخاف with the b- prefix.

exercises.tip: "الضلمة" = the dark, with a d sound.

exercises.prompt: أكمل: "_____ بنلعب كورة في الحارة." المعنى: We used to play football in the alley.

too_formal.feedback: Without the b- prefix the habit sounds bookish; Egyptians add ب before the verb.

exercises.prompt: أكمل: "كل صيف كنا بنروح عند جدي في _____." المعنى: Every summer we went to my grandfather's in the village.

too_formal.feedback: القرية is the MSA word; a countryside village is simply البلد.

exercises.tip: "البلد" is the village or home town; also the town centre.

exercises.prompt: ترجم: "The first bike I had was red."
exercises.answer: أَوَّل عَجَلَة كَانِت عِنْدِي كَانِت حَمْرَا
accepted: أَوَّل عَجَلَة كَانِت عِنْدِي كَانِت حَمْرَا
أول عجلة كانت عندي كانت حمراء

too_formal.feedback: دراجة and حمراء are MSA; the spoken words are عجلة and حمرا.

exercises.prompt: ترجم: "When I was young I loved to play outside."
exercises.answer: لَمَّا كُنْت صُغَيِّر كُنْت بَاحِب أَلْعَب بَرَّه
accepted: لَمَّا كُنْت صُغَيِّر كُنْت بَاحِب أَلْعَب بَرَّه
lamma kunt soghayyar kunt ba7ebb el3ab barra
وأنا صغير كنت باحب ألعب بره
لما كنت صغير كنت باحب ألعب برة

too_formal.item: عندما كنت صغيرا كنت أحب اللعب في الخارج
too_formal.feedback: عندما and في الخارج are MSA; Cairo says لما and بره.

exercises.prompt: أي جملة معناها "We used to walk to school together every day"؟
exercises.answer: كُنَّا بِنْرُوح المدرسة مَشِي سَوَا كُل يُوم
accepted: كُنَّا بِنْرُوح المدرسة مَشِي سَوَا كُل يُوم
kunna benro7 el-madrasa mashi sawa kull yoom
كنا بنروح المدرسة سوا كل يوم
options: كُنَّا بِنْرُوح المدرسة مَشِي سَوَا كُل يُوم

too_formal.item: كنا نذهب إلى المدرسة معا كل يوم
too_formal.feedback: MSA is fine but spoken Egyptian uses بنروح and سوا.

exercises.prompt: أي جملة معناها "Back then life was much simpler"؟

too_formal.item: في ذلك الوقت كانت الحياة أبسط بكثير
too_formal.feedback: Correct but written; الدنيا and بكتير are the spoken words.

exercises.tip: "الدنيا" = life, the world; "بكتير" = by a lot.

exercises.prompt: رتب الجملة: (My grandmother used to tell us stories before sleeping)
exercises.answer: تِيتَة كَانِت بِتْحَكِّيلَنَا حَوَادِيت قَبْل اَلنَّوْم
accepted: تِيتَة كَانِت بِتْحَكِّيلَنَا حَوَادِيت قَبْل اَلنَّوْم

too_formal.item: جدتي كانت تحكي لنا قصصا قبل النوم
too_formal.feedback: جدتي and قصصا are bookish; تيتة and حواديت are what is said.

exercises.prompt: رتب الجملة: (I had a friend named Kareem)

too_formal.feedback: لدي and يدعى are MSA; Egyptians use عندي and اسمه.

reply.english: Oh no! Will you get it fixed?

dialogue.speaker: Nour
dialogue.arabic: مالك يا سامي؟ شكلك مضايق.
dialogue.transliteration: maalak ya saami? shaklak medaya2.
dialogue.english: What's wrong Sami? You look upset.

dialogue.speaker: Sami
dialogue.arabic: يا ستار، إمبارح كان يوم وحش. الموبايل بتاعي باظ.
dialogue.transliteration: ya sattaar, imbaare7 kaan yoom wi7esh. el-mobayl bitaa3i baaz.
dialogue.english: Oh dear, yesterday was a bad day. My phone broke.

dialogue.speaker: Nour
dialogue.arabic: يا خبر! وهتصلحه؟
dialogue.transliteration: ya khabar! w-hatSallaho?
dialogue.english: Oh no! And will you fix it?

dialogue.speaker: Sami
dialogue.arabic: أكيد. وبعدها ضيعت مفتاح البيت.
dialogue.transliteration: akeed. w-ba3daha Dayya3t miftaa7 el-beet.
dialogue.english: Of course. And after that I lost the house key.

dialogue.speaker: Nour
dialogue.arabic: لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله! ودخلت إزاي؟
dialogue.transliteration: laa 7awla wala 2uwwa illa billah! w-dakhalt ezzay?
dialogue.english: There is no power but with God! And how did you get in?

dialogue.speaker: Sami
dialogue.arabic: استنيت أخويا لحد ما جه. وفي الصبح اتأخرت على الشغل.
dialogue.transliteration: istanneet akhuuya la7add ma gah. w-fis-Sob7 it2akhkhart 3ala esh-shoghl.
dialogue.english: I waited for my brother until he came. And in the morning I was late for work.

dialogue.speaker: Nour
dialogue.arabic: ليه؟ العربية عطلت؟
dialogue.transliteration: leeh? el-3arabiyya 3eTlit?
dialogue.english: Why? Did the car break down?

dialogue.speaker: Sami
dialogue.arabic: لا، نمت زيادة ومسمعتش المنبه.
dialogue.transliteration: laa, nimt ziyaada w-masme3tesh el-monabbeh.
dialogue.english: No, I overslept and didn't hear the alarm.

dialogue.speaker: Nour
dialogue.arabic: وبعدين؟ حصل حاجة تانية؟
dialogue.transliteration: w-ba3deen? 7aSal 7aaga tanya?
dialogue.english: And then? Did anything else happen?

dialogue.speaker: Sami
dialogue.arabic: وقعت على السلم وعورت رجلي، والقهوة اتكبت على اللابتوب.
dialogue.transliteration: we2e3t 3ala es-sillim wa3awwart reggli, w-el-2ahwa itkabbit 3ala el-laptop.
dialogue.english: I fell on the stairs and hurt my leg, and coffee spilled on the laptop.

dialogue.speaker: Nour
dialogue.arabic: يا حرام! ألف سلامة على رجلك.
dialogue.transliteration: ya 7aram! alf salaama 3ala riglak.
dialogue.english: Poor you! I hope your leg gets better soon.

dialogue.speaker: Sami
dialogue.arabic: الله يسلمك. المهم إنها عدت على خير.
dialogue.transliteration: allah yisallimik. el-muhimm innaha 3adit 3ala kheer.
dialogue.english: God keep you. What matters is that it passed well.

pair.english: Why were you late this morning?

response.english: I overslept and didn't hear the alarm.
It got lost at the airport.

lessons.culture: When something breaks Egyptians say باظ or عطل, and after a mishap the comfort is المهم إنها عدت على خير. Someone who got hurt or had a bad day is told ألف سلامة or سلامتك.

exercises.prompt: صاحبك بيقولك: "الموبايل بتاعي باظ إمبارح.". رد عليه.

too_formal.feedback: Correct but bookish; يا خبر with the plain question هتصلحه is how a friend answers.

exercises.tip: "هـ" before a verb is the future: هتصلحه = will you fix it.

exercises.prompt: صاحبك بيسألك: "إيدك مالها؟". جاوبه إنك جرحت إيدك وإنت بتطبخ.

too_formal.feedback: أثناء الطبخ is written style; وأنا باطبخ is the spoken way.

exercises.prompt: أكمل: "الموبايل بتاعي _____ إمبارح." المعنى: My phone broke yesterday.

too_formal.feedback: انكسر means physically snapped; for a phone that broke down Cairo says باظ.

exercises.tip: "باظ" = it broke down, it got spoiled; the z here stands for ظ.

exercises.prompt: أكمل: "نمت زيادة و_____ المنبه." المعنى: I overslept and didn't hear the alarm.

too_formal.feedback: لم is MSA; the spoken negative is ما + verb + ش.

exercises.tip: "مسمعتش" = I didn't hear; ما + verb + ش is the Egyptian negative.

exercises.prompt: ترجم: "I lost the house key."

too_formal.feedback: فقدت is MSA and منزل bookish; Egyptians say ضيعت and البيت.

exercises.prompt: ترجم: "The car broke down in the middle of the road."

too_formal.feedback: السيارة and منتصف are MSA; Cairo says العربية and نص.

exercises.prompt: أي جملة معناها "I forgot my wallet at home"؟

too_formal.feedback: Correct MSA, but Egyptians say المحفظة and البيت.

exercises.prompt: أي جملة معناها "My bag got lost at the airport"؟

too_formal.feedback: حقيبتي is MSA; Cairo says شنطتي.

exercises.prompt: رتب الجملة: (I fell on the stairs and hurt my leg)

too_formal.feedback: سقطت and ساقي are MSA; وقعت and رجلي are spoken.

exercises.prompt: رتب الجملة: (Coffee spilled on my laptop)

too_formal.feedback: انسكبت and حاسوبي are MSA; the passive is اتكبت, and اللابتوب is the everyday word.

phrases.arabic: لِسَّه مِش مِتَأَكِّدِين، مُمْكِن يَكُون إِشَاعَة بَس
phrases.transliteration: lissa mesh met2akkideen, mumken yekoon ishaa3a bass

phrases.arabic: مِش هَتْصَدِّق إِيه اَللِّي حَصَل إِمْبَارِح فِي اَلْحِتَّة
phrases.transliteration: mesh hatSaddaq eh elli 7aSal imbaare7 fil-7etta

reply.english: May God keep him for them.

phrases.arabic: مَتْقُولِش لِحَد، بَس سِمِعْت إِنْهُم هَيْسَافِرُوا
phrases.transliteration: matu2oolsh le-7add, bass smi3t innuhum hayesaafru

phrases.arabic: ده كُلُّه كَلَام نَاس، مَعْرَفِش صِح وَلَّا لَأ
phrases.transliteration: da kullu kalaam naas, ma3rafsh Sa7 walla la2

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.arabic: أهلا هبة، إيه آخر أخبارك؟
dialogue.transliteration: ahlan Heba, eh aakhir akhbaarik?
dialogue.english: Hi Heba, what's your latest news?

dialogue.speaker: Heba
dialogue.arabic: الحمد لله، كله تمام. في خبر مش هتصدقيه!
dialogue.transliteration: el-7amdu lillah, kullu tamaam. fee khabar mesh hatSaddaqeeh!
dialogue.english: Thank God, all is well. There's news you won't believe!

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.arabic: إيه هو؟ قولي بسرعة!
dialogue.transliteration: eh huwwa? 2ooli bi-sur3a!
dialogue.english: What is it? Tell me quickly!

dialogue.speaker: Heba
dialogue.arabic: سمعت إن سامر اتخطب.
dialogue.transliteration: smi3t inn saamer itkhaTab.
dialogue.english: I heard that Samer got engaged.

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.arabic: بجد؟ مين قالك الخبر ده؟
dialogue.transliteration: begad? meen 2aalik el-khabar da?
dialogue.english: Really? Who told you this news?

dialogue.speaker: Heba
dialogue.arabic: أختي قالتلي. وبالمناسبة أختي اتجوزت الشهر اللي فات.
dialogue.transliteration: ukhti 2aalitli. w-bil-monaasba ukhti itgawwizit esh-shahr elli faat.
dialogue.english: My sister told me. And by the way, my sister got married last month.

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.arabic: ألف مبروك! وسمعنا إن جارتنا خلفت ولد.
dialogue.transliteration: alf mabrook! w-sme3na inn gaartina khallafit walad.
dialogue.english: A thousand congratulations! And we heard our neighbour had a baby boy.

dialogue.speaker: Heba
dialogue.arabic: ربنا يخليه لهم. وقالولي إنك هتنقلي لبيت جديد.
dialogue.transliteration: rabbena yekhalleeh lohom. w-2aloolee innik hatin2eli le-beet gedeed.
dialogue.english: May God keep him for them. And they told me you're moving to a new house.

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.arabic: لسه مش متأكدة، ممكن يكون إشاعة بس. بيقولوا إن محل فلان قفل كمان.
dialogue.transliteration: lissa mesh met2akkida, mumken yekoon ishaa3a bass. biy2oolu inn ma7all folaan 2afal kamaan.
dialogue.english: I'm not sure yet, it might just be a rumor. They're saying such-and-such shop closed too.

dialogue.speaker: Heba
dialogue.arabic: متقوليش لحد، بس سمعت إنهم هيسافروا.
dialogue.transliteration: matu2oolish le-7add, bass smi3t innuhum hayesaafru.
dialogue.english: Don't tell anyone, but I heard they're going to travel.

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.arabic: ده كله كلام ناس، معرفش صح ولا لأ.
dialogue.transliteration: da kullu kalaam naas, ma3rafsh Sa7 walla la2.
dialogue.english: That's all just people's talk, I don't know if it's true or not.

dialogue.speaker: Heba
dialogue.arabic: معاكي حق. خلينا نستنى ونشوف.
dialogue.transliteration: ma3aaki 7a2. khalleena nistanna wa-nshoof.
dialogue.english: You're right. Let's wait and see.

response.english: A friend of mine told me.

pair.english: When did your sister get married?

response.english: I don't know, it might be a rumor.

lessons.culture: For good news such as an engagement, wedding or new baby Egyptians answer ألف مبروك, and for a baby ربنا يخليه لكم. When news is not certain they say كلام ناس, and متقولش لحد keeps gossip from spreading.

exercises.prompt: صاحبتك بتقولك: "أختي اتجوزت الشهر اللي فات.". رد عليها.

too_formal.feedback: أبارك لك is written; the spoken answer is ألف مبروك.

exercises.tip: "ألف مبروك" is the standard answer to good news.

exercises.prompt: صاحبك بيسألك: "مين قالك الخبر ده؟". جاوبه إن أختك قالتلك.

too_formal.feedback: أخبرتني is MSA; قالتلي is what is said.

exercises.prompt: أكمل: "سمعت _____ سامر اتخطب." المعنى: I heard that Samer got engaged.

too_formal.feedback: The spoken word for "that" here is إن, said inn.

exercises.prompt: أكمل: "ده كله كلام _____." المعنى: That's all just people's talk.

too_formal.feedback: Both are heard; كلام ناس is the fixed everyday phrase.

exercises.prompt: ترجم: "Who told you this news?" (تكلم راجل)

too_formal.feedback: من and هذا are MSA; Cairo says مين and ده.

exercises.prompt: ترجم: "What's the latest news with you?"

too_formal.feedback: ما is MSA; إيه is the spoken "what".

exercises.tip: "إيه أخبارك" is also a common greeting.

exercises.prompt: أي جملة معناها "They told me you're moving to a new house"؟

too_formal.item: أخبروني أنك ستنتقل إلى منزل جديد
too_formal.feedback: ستنتقل is written; the spoken future is هـ + verb.

exercises.prompt: أي جملة معناها "Don't tell anyone"؟

too_formal.feedback: لا تخبر is MSA; the spoken command is ما + verb + ش.

exercises.prompt: رتب الجملة: (They're saying that such-and-such shop closed)

too_formal.feedback: يقولون and أغلق are MSA; بيقولوا and قفل are spoken.

exercises.prompt: رتب الجملة: (I heard that Samer got engaged)

too_formal.feedback: MSA خطب is written; the spoken passive is اتخطب.

challenge.title: Tell Me What Happened
challenge.instructions: Write and say a short Egyptian conversation of at least 10 lines between two people catching up. It must include asking what happened yesterday, an answer in the past tense, a childhood memory, one thing that went wrong, and one piece of news or gossip you heard. Use at least 8 target phrases from Unit 16 and include both a masculine-address form and a feminine-address form.
required_elements: A question about yesterday using إمبارح and عملت إيه or حصل إيه.
An answer describing something that happened, using a past-tense verb.
A memory from childhood using لما كنت صغير or كنا بـ.
Something that went wrong, using a word like باظ, ضيعت, or اتأخرت.
A piece of news or gossip introduced with سمعت إن or قالولي.
At least one masculine-address form such as عملت or شفت.
At least one feminine-address form such as عملتي or شفتي.
A closing reaction such as يا خبر, يا حرام, or ألف سلامة.

dialogue.speaker: Bilal
dialogue.arabic: منى، عاملة إيه؟ إمبارح عملتي إيه؟
dialogue.transliteration: Mona, 3amla eh? imbaare7 3amalti eh?
dialogue.english: Mona, how are you? What did you do yesterday?

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.arabic: أهلا بلال، مش هتصدق اللي حصل معايا إمبارح!
dialogue.transliteration: ahlan Bilal, mesh hatSaddaq elli 7aSal ma3aaya imbaare7!
dialogue.english: Hi Bilal, you won't believe what happened to me yesterday!

dialogue.speaker: Bilal
dialogue.arabic: إيه؟ قوليلي!
dialogue.transliteration: eh? 2ooleeli!
dialogue.english: What? Tell me!

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.arabic: الموبايل بتاعي باظ وضيعت مفتاح البيت في نفس اليوم.
dialogue.transliteration: el-mobayl bitaa3i baaz w-Dayya3t miftaa7 el-beet fee nafs el-yoom.
dialogue.english: My phone broke and I lost the house key on the same day.

dialogue.speaker: Bilal
dialogue.arabic: يا خبر! يوم زي ده فكرني بأيام المدرسة.
dialogue.transliteration: ya khabar! yoom zayy da fakkarni be-ayyaam el-madrasa.
dialogue.english: Oh no! A day like that reminds me of school days.

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.arabic: صح، لما كنا صغيرين كنا بنروح المدرسة مشي سوا كل يوم.
dialogue.transliteration: Sa7, lamma kunna Soghayyareen kunna benro7 el-madrasa mashi sawa kull yoom.
dialogue.english: True, when we were young we walked to school together every day.

dialogue.speaker: Bilal
dialogue.arabic: وكنتي بتخافي من الضلمة، فاكرة؟
dialogue.transliteration: w-kunti bet-khaafi min iD-Dalma, fakra?
dialogue.english: And you were afraid of the dark, remember?

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.arabic: هههه آه! بس إنت شفت مين إمبارح؟
dialogue.transliteration: hahaha aah! bass inta shuft meen imbaare7?
dialogue.english: Haha yes! But who did you see yesterday?

dialogue.speaker: Bilal
dialogue.arabic: شفت سامي، وقالي إن أخته اتجوزت الشهر اللي فات.
dialogue.transliteration: shuft saami, w-2aali inn ukhtu itgawwizit esh-shahr elli faat.
dialogue.english: I saw Sami, and he told me his sister got married last month.

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.arabic: ده كلام ناس، نستنى ونشوف. ألف سلامة عليكي، وربنا يعوضك.
dialogue.transliteration: da kalaam naas, nistanna wa-nshoof. alf salaama 3aleeki, w-rabbena ye3awwaDik.
dialogue.english: That's just talk, let's wait and see. Sorry about your day, and may God make it up to you.

dialogue.speaker: Bilal
dialogue.arabic: ده كلام ناس، نستنى ونشوف. ألف سلامة عليكي من يوم إمبارح!
dialogue.transliteration: da kalaam naas, nistanna wa-nshoof. alf salaama 3aleeki min yoom imbaare7!
dialogue.english: That's just talk, let's wait and see. Get well from yesterday!
